findings.claim: 'Claude Code uses mcp_tool and starts no process' is only true for PreToolUse. Claude Code skips mcp_tool hooks on SessionStart at launch/--continue/--resume, so that hook must be type command and pays bare Node startup (45.6 ms p95). The GS6 split (command agents vs Claude Code) leaves Claude Code SessionStart with no budget, and PRD:102 still says every hook is one command entry.
findings.evidence: /tmp/wf4/doc-hooks.md:590 'SessionStart at launch, including with --continue or --resume ... Claude Code skips their mcp_tool hooks without calling the tool ... For anything the session needs at launch, use a type: "command" hook'. ADR-0009:117 'the whole SessionStart process is 48.6 ms p95'. PRD-v2.md:102 'One entry: context-mode hook <agent> <event>'.
findings.fix: Add a per-event transport row for Claude Code in the adapter table (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart(compact|clear): mcp_tool; SessionStart(startup|resume): command) and give GS6 one budget per transport.

findings.claim: GP3 hook-runner only spawns a hook process and times it. The mcp_tool path (Claude Code, the reference agent) has no harness: no timing of the route tool inside the server, no test of the 'server still connecting' wait, no test of hook timeout fail-open. A stalled mcp_tool PreToolUse waits up to MCP_TIMEOUT within a 600 s default timeout, and a timed-out hook lets the tool run.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:251 'hook-runner.mjs spawn hook entry with a recorded native payload on stdin; capture stdout, exit code, wall time'. doc-hooks.md:426 'Defaults: 600 for command, http, and mcp_tool'; :584 'waits for a connecting server ... for at most MCP_TIMEOUT'; :878 'A timed-out ... mcp_tool hook doesn't block the tool call'.
findings.fix: Add a GP3 mcp_tool lane: harness/mcp-client.mjs calls the route tool with recorded tool_input and asserts p95 in-server time; set an explicit short timeout on the generated mcp_tool entries and document fail-open as the one path.

findings.claim: With mcp_tool, every Claude Code PreToolUse decision runs on the MCP server's event loop. node:sqlite DatabaseSync is synchronous; with {timeout: 5000} a lock wait blocks that loop for up to 5 s, and large index transactions block it ~108 ms p99. Every tool call of the session then stalls behind it. This is the #985 symptom class (sync busy wait freezes the loop). No doc puts the route decision or the hint/ready-row DB access off the main loop or bounds it.
findings.evidence: ADR-0002:21 'node:sqlite with {timeout: 5000}'. tickets/verify-single-db.md:11 'its sync busy_timeout (30000 ms) freezes the event loop at low CPU'; :16 '1 MB index tx p50 24 ms, p99 108 ms ... fails with database is locked after about 5.2 s'. ADR-0008:30 'Hints once per session are keyed by session_id in context.db'.
findings.fix: State that the route tool does no blocking DB write on the request path (hint marker in memory per server + async journal), or runs DB work in a worker; add GP8 case: route p95 while a 20 MB index runs and while another process holds the write lock.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 7afa0f45 2026-05-19 'fix(db-base): propagate busy_timeout on node:sqlite branch (closes #642)'; 13dcec21 2026-04-02 'fix: handle SQLITE_BUSY with retry logic and graceful errors (closes #218)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: src/db-base.ts:300 'node:sqlite's DatabaseSync constructor silently ignores { timeout } ... Without this, the default is 0'. REGRESSION_RISK: dropping busy_timeout re-breaks #642/#218 (instant 'database is locked'); keeping it sync on the server loop re-creates the #985 freeze for hooks. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep busy_timeout via PRAGMA, keep BEGIN IMMEDIATE, keep hook path free of waits.

findings.claim: Parallel batches fire PreToolUse hooks concurrently. 'Hints once per session keyed by session_id in context.db' gives no atomic claim, so N parallel Read/Grep calls can each see 'not shown' and each inject the hint (the #1267 class). v1 solved the race with an O_EXCL create-or-fail marker.
findings.evidence: doc-hooks.md:412 'All matching hooks run in parallel'; :2289 'PostToolUse fires once per tool, which means it fires concurrently when Claude makes parallel tool calls'. tickets/data/isall.json #1267 'guidanceOnce("read") ... re-injects the Read tip on every Read'. v1 hooks/core/routing.mjs:130-131 'Atomic create-or-fail: O_CREAT | O_EXCL ... First process to create the file wins'.
findings.fix: Specify the claim as one atomic statement (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING in BEGIN IMMEDIATE, or an in-server Set for mcp_tool) and add a GP3 case: 8 parallel Read hooks in one session yield exactly 1 hint.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: dfe38d94 2026-03-13 'fix: throttle advisory PreToolUse guidance to once-per-session (#113)' (git blame routing.mjs:130-131). ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'Hybrid throttle: in-memory Set (same-process) + file-based markers ... deny/modify actions are never throttled.' REGRESSION_RISK: non-atomic check-then-write re-breaks #113 under parallel batches. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: atomic first-writer-wins; denies stay unthrottled (ADR-0008 #7 keeps this).

findings.claim: 'PostToolUse runs async where the host allows it' conflicts with ADR-0016 case C, which needs PostToolUse updatedToolOutput to keep large output out of subagent context (owner MUST). Claude Code ignores decision fields of async hooks. Also in -p mode async hooks are killed at teardown, so journal rows (and E2E evidence) can be lost.
findings.evidence: doc-hooks.md:3995 'Async hooks can't block or control Claude's behavior: response fields like decision, permissionDecision, and continue have no effect'; :4026 'with the -p flag, Claude Code kills any async hook still running at teardown'. ADR-0016:28 case C 'PostToolUse updatedToolOutput (Claude Code, all tools)'.
findings.fix: PostToolUse is synchronous wherever it may replace output (case C tools); async only for pure journal entries on non-replace matchers, and E2E must not depend on async rows.

findings.claim: 'about 12 KB, 1.26 ms in the server' attributes 1.26 ms to the v2 parser. The 1.26 ms was the ctx_route call on a stub server; the parser prototype measured 3.9 ms first parse and 0.31 ms warm. On the command-hook path the proposed '<= 20 ms CPU on top of bare Node' was measured only as a median (parse+sql 48.8 vs 33.1 ms), never at p95 and never on Windows.
findings.evidence: tickets/round4-evidence.json F13 'server.log {"ev":"route","ms":1.256166 ...}' (stub server); F4 '{"load_ms":0.457,"parse1_ms":3.944,"warm_ms":0.312}' and 'empty cpu median 33.1 p90 39.0 ... sql cpu median 48.8 p90 54.0'.
findings.fix: Quote the parser numbers from F4 (cold 3.9 ms, warm 0.3 ms) and mark the 20 ms CPU proposal [U] until GP3 measures p95 on the 3 CI OSes.
